headline: North American ferrous scrap benchmarks rise $10-15 a ton
detail: All seven tracked North American steel scrap grades rose on Nov 12, led by shredded auto scrap up $15/MT and busheling, HMS and bundles up $10/MT. It signals firm mill demand heading into December ferrous trade.

headline: Clean copper scrap grades drop 11 cents a pound Friday
detail: Bare bright, #1 and #2 copper and light copper each fell 11 cents/lb on Nov 13, with brass down 3 cents and EC aluminum wire down 1 cent; steel grades were flat. Yard buy prices for red metal are under pressure as the futures slide continues.

headline: Copper futures sink to near five-month low around $6 a pound
detail: COMEX copper fell toward $6.00/lb Monday, the lowest since June, as AI-stock selling, a stronger dollar on bets of aggressive Fed hikes and LME stocks near 320,000 t weighed. Lower copper means weaker scrap bids for #1 and #2.

headline: December Fed hike now seen as near certain after hot CPI
detail: Markets priced about a 91% chance of a December rate hike after October CPI rose 0.4%, and Fed Governor Waller floated a half-point move; the dollar index held near 102.2. A firm dollar and higher rates weigh on copper, gold and other dollar-priced metals.

headline: US raw steel output drops 13% in one week
detail: AISI data showed US mills made 1.778 million tons in the week to Nov 7 at 77% utilization, down from 88.9% the week before, though year-to-date output is up 5.9%. Lower mill run rates can trim near-term scrap buying.

headline: Cleveland-Cliffs reaches four-year labor deal with USW
detail: Cliffs agreed new contracts covering about 12,000 steelworkers at plants and mines in Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Minnesota and Michigan, pending ratification. It removes a strike risk for a major Midwest steelmaker while US Steel talks continue.

headline: Aluminum squeeze deepens as LME stocks hit lowest since 1990
detail: LME aluminum inventories are down 56% this year and spot metal traded $92/t over three-month futures, with Gulf supply disrupted by the Middle East war and China capping output. Tight nearby supply supports premiums and aluminum scrap values.

headline: Gold breaks below $4,000 in a losing week for precious metals
detail: Spot gold fell below $4,000 on Nov 12, touching about $3,852, and steadied near $3,880-3,897 Friday as a stronger dollar and Fed-hike worries weighed. Weaker gold cuts payouts on karat scrap.

headline: Palladium bounces 1.6% Friday to about $1,008 after Thursday's 5% drop
detail: Trading Economics shows palladium closing Nov 13 near $1,007.50, up from $991.50, though other dealer quotes were weaker. Converter values are still well below where they were early last week.

headline: Platinum slips back from two-week high
detail: Platinum fell below $1,530/oz on Nov 13 as stalled US-Iran talks kept oil high and fed expectations of more Fed tightening. Weaker vehicle output and the EV shift remain headwinds for converter-grade metal demand.

headline: Record Chinese import premiums show tight physical copper
detail: Copper briefly rebounded toward $6.30/lb as China's import premiums hit records and smelters cut output on high ore costs, with metal diverted to the US ahead of possible tariffs. Physical tightness in China could limit how far prices fall.

headline: Brazil pig iron exports fall on weak US demand
detail: Brazil shipped 317,200 t of pig iron in October, down 6.6% from September, with 174,700 t going to the US at about $452/t FOB. Softer US pig iron buying is a read on EAF raw material demand alongside prime scrap.

headline: Iron ore slides as Hebei steel curbs loom
detail: Dalian iron ore fell toward CNY 670/t, a one-week low, as Tangshan and Handan entered winter pollution controls and Chinese hot metal output kept falling. Weaker Chinese steel output pressures global steel and scrap export prices.

headline: Aluminum rebounds to $3,050 but overseas Chinese capacity caps gains
detail: Aluminum futures recovered to about $3,050/t after testing year lows below $3,000, while the LME prompt spread hit a five-month high of $94/t. Chinese-backed smelters abroad, led by Indonesia, are adding over 15 million t of capacity that keeps longer-term prices in check.

headline: Habas mill blast toll rises to 17, six detained
detail: Six people were detained after the Nov 9 explosion at Habas's Aliaga steel plant in Turkey killed 17 workers, and President Erdogan promised a full probe. An extended outage at a top Turkish scrap buyer could soften deep-sea scrap demand.

headline: Honda plans $3 billion new auto plant in Ohio
detail: Honda will build a 240,000-vehicle plant in central Ohio starting production in 2029 and expand hybrid powertrain capacity there by 250%. More Midwest auto output means more prompt industrial scrap down the road.

headline: China factory-gate prices up 5.7% as nonferrous costs soar
detail: China's October PPI rose 5.7% from a year earlier, with nonferrous metal purchase prices up 16.7% while ferrous metal prices fell 1.1%. It shows strong base metal costs alongside a weak steel market in China.
source: National Bureau of Statistics of China

headline: Chinese copper scrap prices edge higher
detail: China's #1 bare bright and copper wire scrap rose CNY 300/t on Nov 13, while aluminum and steel scrap held flat. Firm Chinese scrap bids reflect short refined supply there, a support for US export copper scrap.

headline: Chinese mills cut crude steel output 7% in late October
detail: CISA member mills averaged 1.76 million t/day of crude steel from Oct 21-31, down 7% from mid-month, as demand stayed slack and finished steel stocks fell 13.5%. Lower Chinese output reduces iron ore demand and steel export pressure.

headline: Worldsteel now sees global steel demand shrinking in 2026
detail: The World Steel Association cut its 2026 forecast to a 0.1% contraction and expects China's steel use to fall 2% on a longer property slump, as rebar futures fell toward CNY 3,030/t. A weaker global steel outlook caps scrap price upside.

headline: European mills cut scrap prices about 10 euros a ton
detail: Scrap buying prices fell in Germany, France, Austria, Switzerland, Italy and Spain in November, mostly by 10-15 euros/t, as high energy costs forced mills to cut or halt production. Weaker European scrap demand can redirect export tonnage.

headline: Copper rebounds as Freeport approves $4.5 billion Arizona expansion
detail: COMEX copper bounced about 1.9% to near $6.36/lb on Nov 9 as Shanghai stocks hit a near three-year low, while Freeport approved a $4.5 billion expansion of its Bagdad mine in Arizona. COMEX stocks remain more than double a year ago.

headline: US sets preliminary duties on Turkish tin mill steel
detail: Commerce found preliminary dumping margins of 42.06% for one exporter and 3.89% for Tosyali Toyo and all others on tinplate and tin-free steel from Turkey, with a final ruling due within 75 days. It extends trade protection for US flat steel.

headline: Central bank gold buying on pace to beat 2025
detail: World Gold Council data show official purchases of 321 t in Q3, 42% above a year earlier, with year-to-date buying 6% ahead of 2025, Heraeus noted. Steady central bank demand helps cushion gold against Fed-hike pressure.
